page: Amazon Web Services c5n.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance provisioned on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, engineered for network-intensive compute tasks. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache allocation includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 24 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 42.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing approximately 2.62 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance incorporates a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local storage is bundled, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and it contains no discrete GPUs.

Performance benchmarks show consistent mid-tier capabilities across multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth, alongside weaker single-core compute results. Multi-core testing recorded 14,808.85 on stress-ng and 7,317.0 on Geekbench multi-core, alongside a score of 12,685.0 in software compilation using Clang. In contrast, stress-ng single-core performance reached 1,407.28, falling into the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth recorded 89.55 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 45.22 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, Redis achieved 13.96 million SET operations per second, and static web serving reached 11.58 GB/sec. Prompt processing for a 7B parameter language model registered at 24.09 tokens per second, placing it in the lower quartile for that task.

From an architectural standpoint, the c5n.4xlarge prioritizes network bandwidth and compute density over onboard storage. The absence of local NVMe disks avoids bundled drive expenses for environments that rely purely on centralized storage or network data pipelines. The configuration is suited for network-heavy compute tasks, distributed continuous integration and software build pipelines, web serving clusters, and batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, it includes 42.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz and delivers 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark data reflects average multi-core and memory performance, registering 7,317.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 14,808.85 in stress-ng multi-core, with single-core processing testing in the lower quartile. Memory throughput achieves 89.55 GB/sec for uncached reads, supporting 13.96 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.58 GB/sec in static web throughput. This hardware profile supports network-bound compute workloads, build farms, and batch data processing.
